answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut mandate and 14-day contract expiration create urgency, but the 94% line utilization leaves no margin for supply disruption. Switching vendors (memory_c2) worked before but risks onboarding friction under tight timelines. A second source (memory_c3) is the safest long-term hedge but doesn't address the immediate 18% cost target. Renewing (memory_c1) preserves stability but forfeits the cost reduction opportunity. Deferring (memory_c5) is not viable—the contract expires in 14 days without auto-renewal. Negotiating_terms is the highest-leverage move: memory_c4 shows benchmarking recovered real margin at renewal, and memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing. A renegotiation targeting both price reduction and volume commitment can hit the 18% cost target while keeping the incumbent's proven integration and delivery reliability in place—critical with 94% utilization. This approach preserves the option to add a second source later if negotiations fail, and it does not force a risky vendor switch during a constrained period.
